complexity.notes: Correct but very slow: `sorted(subset) not in result` scans up to 2^n stored subsets of length n for every one of the 2^n masks, pushing the real cost to O(n * 4^n) — the benchmark model field has no 4^n form, so 'n 2^n' there is the output-size bound, not the true runtime. Sorting each subset repeatedly is also wasted work. An O(n * 2^n) approach exists: ||sort nums once, then backtrack, skipping over duplicate values at the same recursion level so each distinct subset is generated exactly once||. Minor style point: f-string bit formatting works but `i >> j & 1` or itertools would be more idiomatic.
complexity.summary: Enumerates all 2^n bitmasks, builds each subset, and appends it only if its sorted form is not already in the result list, deduplicating via a linear membership scan.
